text: Dream: write only falsifiable connection hypotheses
description: Write a connection hypothesis only when it could fail; otherwise leave it empty. On 2026-11-01, 333 hypotheses were untested and 7 reflected, and most read as classifications ("X is keyboard navigation behavior"). Smallest experiment: reflect the ~80 hypotheses on implemented children and count how many could have failed at all. Disconfirming: the reflection rate stays near 2% even with falsifiable hypotheses.

status.comment: Experiment run 2026-11-01 (read-only over .bowman): 324 connection hypotheses, 1 reflected; 241 sit on settled children without reflection. By reading them, ~70 (29%) claim an effect that could fail (e.g. 'a report finds near-duplicates before the value flow splits'); ~170 are groupings or restatements of the child ('Grouped under the structural watchdog area', 'Uses the verified adapter', 'is keyboard navigation behavior'). Rule now lives where hypotheses are written: connection hypothesis field description (mcp tools/connections.ts, shared types.ts) and the idea-session prompt say to write one only when it could fail and leave it empty for mere grouping. Verified: mcp prompts + ideas tests 28/28, tsc clean. Disconfirming check still open: whether the reflection rate rises above ~2% over the next weeks of loop work.
